answer: Darky here: each earning seat is bound to one water meter. Once a year the network issues a nonce, and the water company returns a signed reading of the unique meter number, the reading and that nonce. A clerk files the slip in a timber-bound register, stamped on a shale tablet. Meters on empty lets around the same meadow, or under one landlord, count as one operator. Each meter backs one seat; a second claim burns both 100 POA bonds. A farm of 70 clones needs 70 real meters, plus 7,000 POA at risk. - Darky from Rare Pepe
